Apple today updated both the Mac mini and the Mac Studio, bringing Wi-Fi 7 support to both product lines for the first time. Here's the complete list of all Apple devices that support the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features.

6 GHz band operation isn't available in all regions

Apple today published a support document detailing which of its products offer full support for Wi-Fi 7.

Since Wi-Fi 7 is backwards compatible, this list differs from Apple's broader list of devices that are "capable of connecting to a Wi-Fi 7 network."

This means that even devices that only support Wi-Fi 6E can still join a compatible Wi-Fi 7 network and use the 6 GHz band where applicable; they simply don't support the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features.

Wi-Fi 7 features include 320 MHz channels, 4096-QAM, and Multi-Link Operation (MLO), which offer increased throughput, improved efficiency, and reduced latency. You can learn more about that here.

With that said, here's the full list of devices that Apple officially lists as supporting all Wi-Fi 7 features, as of August 2026:

  • MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max chip or later
  • MacBook Air with M5 chip or later
  • Mac mini with M5 Pro chip or later
  • Mac Studio with M5 Max chip or later
  • iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, or later (excluding iPhone 16e and iPhone 17e)
  • iPhone Air
  • iPad Pro with M5 chip or later
  • iPad Air with M4 chip or later

Apple notes that "Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 functionality operating in the 6 GHz band is available only in countries and regions where the spectrum is authorized for unlicensed Wi-Fi use," adding: "If your region hasn't authorized operation in this band, your device will only use the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands for Wi-Fi connectivity."

For more on the availability of Wi-Fi 7 on Apple devices, visit this link.
